Fragmentum ex commentariis in Osee
ΕΚ ΤΩΝ ΕΙΣ ΤΟΝ ΩΣΕΕ ΕΞΗΓΗΤΙΚΩΝ.
13.825 Ἐπειδὴ τὰ σολοικοειδῶς εἰρημένα κατὰ τὴν Γραφὴν ὅσα κατὰ τὴν λέξιν
συγχύνει τὸν ἐντυγχάνοντα, ὡς ὑπονοεῖν οὐκ ὀρθῶς, οὐδὲ ἀκολούθως, οὐδὲ ὡς ἔχει,
γεγράφθαι τὰ ῥητά· ὡς καὶ τολμᾷν τινας, προφάσει διορθώσεως, ἀλλοιοῦν,
μετατιθέντας τὸν ἐγκείμενον περὶ τὰ δοκοῦντα ἀκολούθως γεγράφθαι ῥητὰ νοῦν·
ἀναγκαίως καὶ ἐνθάδε τοῦ ὁμοίου ἐμπεσόντος, ὅσον κατὰ τὴν λέξιν περὶ τὰ
προκείμενα ῥητὰ, ἴδωμεν τὸν ἐν αὐτοῖς ἐγκείμενον νοῦν. Πληθυντικῶς γὰρ εἰπὼν,
Ἔκλαυσαν καὶ ἐδεήθησάν μου· καὶ πάλιν πληθυντικῶς τὸ ἑξῆς δηλώσας, Ἐν τῷ
οἴκῳ ὢν, εὗρόν με, τὸ ἑξῆς ἐπὶ ἑνικοῦ ἐπιφέρει, λέγων· Καὶ ἐκεῖ ἐλαλήθη πρὸς
αὐτόν. Τῇ γὰρ λέξει ψιλῇ τις ἐνιδὼν κατὰ πλάνην δοκῶν γεγράφθαι, ἢ καὶ τὸ
τελευταῖον πληθυντικῶς γράψει· ἢ τὰ προά 13.828 γοντα εἰς ἑνικὸν μεταθείη.
thought_title: Why Scripture shifts from plural to singular
orientation: Origen opens his commentary by defending the wording of Hosea against readers who think the shift from plural to singular is an error.
pass_a_gloss: Since the things said awkwardly according to the Scripture, as many as according to the wording confuse the reader, so as to suspect not rightly, nor consistently, nor as it is, that the sayings have been written; as also some dare, under pretext of correction, to alter, changing the sense lying in the sayings that seem to have been written consistently; necessarily also here, since the same thing has fallen in, as much as according to the wording concerning the sayings set before us, let us see the sense lying in them. For having said in the plural, 'They wept and besought me'; and again having indicated in the plural what follows, 'Being in the house, they found me', he brings on what follows in the singular, saying: 'And there it was spoken to him.' For someone looking at the bare wording, thinking it has been written by error, will either write the last part in the plural, or will change the preceding parts into the singular.

choices.why: Uses the glossary rendering 'awkward wording' as an adverb with the participle, keeping the literal sense of 'said' rather than a noun.
Keeps the literal 'pretext' and the glossary term 'correction' for διόρθωσις.
Renders ἐγκείμενον literally as 'lying in' to preserve the spatial metaphor of meaning contained in the text.
Literal rendering of the aorist participle of ἐνοράω, emphasizing the act of seeing into the bare wording.
Keeps the literal 'according to error' sense, indicating the mistaken judgment of the reader.
Literal rendering of ψιλῇ as 'bare', preserving the contrast between surface wording and underlying sense.

bible_refs.note: Ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ ὢν, εὗρόν με

pass_b_english: Whenever Scripture says things in awkward wording that confuse the reader at the level of the letter, the reader suspects that the passages have not been written correctly, or consistently, or as they actually stand. Some even dare, under pretext of correction, to alter them, changing the sense that lies in passages which seem to have been written consistently. Since the same thing has occurred here, as far as the letter of the passages before us is concerned, we must look at the sense lying in them.

For the prophet first speaks in the plural: "They wept and begged me." Then he makes the next statement in the plural as well: "Being in the house, they found me." But what follows he brings in the singular, saying, "And there it was spoken to him." Anyone who looks only at the bare wording and thinks it was written by error will either write the last part in the plural or change the preceding parts to the singular.

last_rejected.why: English 'he' obscures that Hosea is the speaker; source uses third person about Hosea. The 'he' refers to Hosea, but this is clear enough from context. No error.
last_rejected.ruling: Reporter concedes 'he' refers to Hosea and is clear from context; λέγων with third person is standard, no meaning lost.

last_rejected.why: 'by error' for κατὰ πλάνην is within normal range (deception/error). No error.
last_rejected.ruling: κατὰ πλάνην rendered 'by error' is within normal range; reporter concedes no error.
